Validation

Use spatially blocked cross-validation to prevent neighboring-region leakage and temporal holdout when repeated periods exist. Compare predictive metrics appropriate to the outcome (RMSE/MAE, log loss, deviance, or calibration). Check residual Moran’s I, posterior predictive checks, overdispersion, influential observations, and coverage of uncertainty intervals. Validate scenario outputs against held-out periods or independent monitoring where available.

## Sensitivity and Robustness

Vary spatial aggregation, exposure transformations, buffer radii, covariate sets, missing-data handling, and spatial-effect specifications. Bootstrap or posterior-sample uncertainty. Re-rank scenarios across plausible intervention reductions, costs, \(\lambda,\rho\), and population-equity weights. Report rank stability rather than a single deterministic winner.

## Falsification

Apply outcome permutations, spatially shifted exposure (“placebo” exposure), negative-control outcomes unlikely to respond to light, and pre-intervention placebo periods. Test whether estimated effects disappear when exposure is randomly reassigned within comparable strata. Examine extreme cases: zero-light areas, saturated radiance, missing covariates, and complete intervention \(r_{ik}\) at its maximum plausible value.

## Reviewer Risks

Primary risks are sampling bias (unequal monitoring and urban coverage), confounded correlation (light proxying population, wealth, or development), ecological fallacy, spatial leakage, arbitrary scenario weights, and omitted uncertainty analysis. These must be explicit limitations.
